ad1e47d6d63694321dac3a0f3775c7b0ae438dd4: A resort on a human scale, Diavolezza focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 35 km of runs are a perfect fit for a 3 to 4 day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to keep changing their playground. Technical terrain is king at Diavolezza: with 23 black and 77 red runs on the programme, confirmed skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are often enjoyed in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. As for snow reliability, Diavolezza is in a strong position with its summit at 3006 m: even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well into April. The village at 2093 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. The budget for a stay at Diavolezza is clearly high: 70€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you need to be aware of it before you go. In short: Diavolezza doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

ada230407985a9e0241079250dbca73c07ec04c4: Fanningberg is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 24 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Fanningberg's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Fanningberg's altitude (1497 m at the base, 2115 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Fanningberg is clearly on the expensive side: €61 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you set off. In short: Fanningberg does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
